title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Wish people well for birthdays, weddings and Odisha’s festivals, give and receive blessings, invite (and insist), and know what to say and do at a wedding.
intro:
Odisha has a saying, **ବାର ମାସରେ ତେର ପର୍ବ** — 'thirteen festivals in twelve months' — and between Rath Yatra, Raja, Durga Puja, Diwali, Nuakhai and the wedding season, there is always something to wish someone well for.

This unit gives you the greetings (**ଜନ୍ମଦିନର ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା**, **ନୂଆଖାଇ ଜୁହାର**), the blessings elders give (**ସୁଖୀ ରୁହ, ଦୀର୍ଘାୟୁ ହୁଅ**), and the grammar behind them — the **wish form** ମଙ୍ଗଳ **ହେଉ** 'may all be well'. You'll also learn to invite the Odia way, which means insisting: **ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବ**, **ନ ଆସିଲେ ମୁଁ ରାଗିବି!**

vocab.note: A synonym of ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା (unit 18), common in messages: ଅନେକ ଶୁଭକାମନା 'best wishes'.
ବିବାହ ବାର୍ଷିକୀ 'wedding anniversary'.

vocab.en: Nuakhai (harvest festival of the new rice, western Odisha)
vocab.note: Lit. 'eating the new (rice)'. Greeting: ନୂଆଖାଇ ଜୁହାର.
Only in wishes and blessings: ମଙ୍ଗଳ ହେଉ, ମଙ୍ଗଳ କରନ୍ତୁ.
ସୁଖରେ ରୁହ 'live happily'. Adjective: ସୁଖୀ 'happy, content'.
Blessing from an elder: ଦୀର୍ଘାୟୁ ହୁଅ 'may you live long'.

vocab.en: respectful greeting to an elder (bowing, touching feet)
vocab.note: ପ୍ରଣାମ କରିବା 'to greet an elder respectfully'; also said aloud: ପ୍ରଣାମ, ଜେଜେମା!
Invitation word: ସପରିବାର ଆସିବେ 'do come with your family'.
ଉପହାର (unit 18) is the Odia word; in speech most people say ଗିଫ୍ଟ.
ବର କନିଆଁ 'the bride and groom'.
Formal: କନ୍ୟା.
The formal agreement between the two families, usually weeks or months before the wedding.
The groom's family and friends who travel with him — dancing, with a band — to the bride's place.
An echo-word pair built on ପର୍ବ (unit 17).
Celebrates the earth and womanhood at the start of the monsoon: swings, new clothes, pitha, no farm work.
The biggest autumn festival; Cuttack is famous for its silver-filigree pandals.
Made for every festival: ପୋଡ଼ପିଠା at Raja, ମଣ୍ଡା, ଏଣ୍ଡୁରି, ଆରିସା…

vocab.en: Mahaprasad (food offered to Jagannath in Puri)
vocab.note: Sacred and shared: you accept it with the right hand and never refuse it.
Cuttack's Bali Jatra (ବାଲିଯାତ୍ରା) is one of the biggest in India.
Colloquially ଦିଆଲି.
ଦୀପ ଜାଳିବା 'to light a lamp'.
ବାଣ ଫୁଟାଇବା 'to set off firecrackers'. (Many people also say ବାଜି, which in unit 29 means 'a bet'.)
କେକ୍ କାଟିବା 'to cut the cake' — the birthday ritual, usually at midnight among friends.

phrases.en: Happy birthday! (lit. many, many good wishes for your birthday)
phrases.note: Friends also just say "Happy birthday" in English.
ଜୁହାର is a respectful greeting used in western Odisha (Sambalpuri).

phrases.en: Be happy and live long. (an elder’s blessing)
May God bless you. (lit. may God do you good)
May you both always be happy. (to a couple)
Please be sure to come with your family.
I'll definitely come — I won't miss it.
Here's a little something for you.
You shouldn't have! (lit. what was the need for all this?)
Give my best wishes to the bride and groom.

phrases.native: ରଜରେ ପିଠା ଖାଇବାକୁ ଆମ ଘରକୁ ଆସିବ।
phrases.roman: Rôjôre piṭha khaibaku amô ghôrôku asibô.
phrases.en: Come over to ours for pitha at Raja.
Shall we go to Cuttack to see the Durga Puja pandals?
phrases.note: ମେଢ଼ = the decorated image of the goddess and its pandal.

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings: ହେଉ, ରୁହ, କରନ୍ତୁ
grammar.body:
Odia wishes and blessings are built from **command forms** — the same ones you know from unit 18 ('let him come': ସେ ଆସୁ).

**1. 'May …' — the third-person wish.** Stem + **-ଉ** (ordinary) or **-ନ୍ତୁ** (respectful or plural subject):
ହେବା → **ହେଉ**: ତୁମର ମଙ୍ଗଳ ହେଉ 'may all go well for you', ତୁମ ଇଚ୍ଛା ପୂରଣ ହେଉ 'may your wishes come true'
ରହିବା → **ରହୁ** · ମିଳିବା → **ମିଳୁ** · ଦେବା → **ଦେଉ**
With God or Jagannath as subject, always respectful **-ନ୍ତୁ**: ଭଗବାନ ତୁମର ମଙ୍ଗଳ **କରନ୍ତୁ**, ମହାପ୍ରଭୁ ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ଭଲରେ **ରଖନ୍ତୁ**.

**2. Blessings from elders — ordinary commands.** Elders bless the young with ତୁମେ / ତୁ commands: **ସୁଖୀ ରୁହ** 'be happy', **ଦୀର୍ଘାୟୁ ହୁଅ** 'live long', **ବଡ଼ ହୁଅ** 'grow up well', **ଶହେ ବର୍ଷ ବଞ୍ଚ** 'live to a hundred' (a birthday favourite). To a couple: **ଦୁହେଁ ଖୁସିରେ ରୁହ**. Note ରହିବା → **ରୁହ**, polite **ରୁହନ୍ତୁ** (like କହିବା → କୁହ, କୁହନ୍ତୁ).

**3. Greetings for an occasion.** Occasion + **-ର** + ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା / ଶୁଭକାମନା / ଅଭିନନ୍ଦନ: ଜନ୍ମଦିନ**ର** ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା, ରଥଯାତ୍ରା**ର** ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା, ବିବାହ ବାର୍ଷିକୀ**ର** ଅଭିନନ୍ଦନ. Or **ଶୁଭ** + occasion: ଶୁଭ ଦୀପାବଳି, ଶୁଭ ବିଜୟା (after Durga Puja). Western Odisha uses **ଜୁହାର**: ନୂଆଖାଇ ଜୁହାର. Reply: **ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, ତୁମକୁ ବି** / **ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ବି**.

**The trap:** don't *command* an elder. To someone older, wish with the respectful form — ଆପଣ ସବୁବେଳେ ସୁସ୍ଥ **ରୁହନ୍ତୁ** — never ~~ସୁଖୀ ରୁହ~~ or ~~ଦୀର୍ଘାୟୁ ହୁଅ~~; those are for elders to say to you. And keep the wish form apart from the future: ମଙ୍ଗଳ **ହେଉ** 'may it be good' vs ମଙ୍ଗଳ **ହେବ** 'it will be good'.

examples.en: May Lord Jagannath keep you well.
Live to a hundred! (birthday blessing from an elder)
May you always stay healthy. (to an elder)

grammar.title: 'Be sure to…' and 'don't forget to…': ନିଶ୍ଚୟ, -ବାକୁ ଭୁଲିବ ନାହିଁ
grammar.body:
Invitations in Odisha are **insistent**. A polite 'come if you can' sounds as if you don't really want the person; hosts push, and guests are expected to be pushed. The tools:

**ନିଶ୍ଚୟ + future** 'be sure to': ନିଶ୍ଚୟ **ଆସିବ** (ଆପଣ: ନିଶ୍ଚୟ **ଆସିବେ**; ତୁ: ନିଶ୍ଚୟ **ଆସିବୁ**). The future is the normal way to invite (unit 17); ନିଶ୍ଚୟ makes it firm. In formal speech **ଅବଶ୍ୟ** (unit 18) does the same.

**-ବାକୁ ଭୁଲିବ ନାହିଁ** 'don't forget to …': ମିଠା ଆଣିବାକୁ ଭୁଲିବ ନାହିଁ; polite ଭୁଲିବେ ନାହିଁ.

**… ତ?** 'won't you?': ଆସିବ ତ? 'you'll come, won't you?'

**-ବାକୁ ହିଁ ପଡ଼ିବ** 'you simply have to': the obligation of unit 15 plus emphatic ହିଁ: ତୁମକୁ ଆସିବାକୁ **ହିଁ** ପଡ଼ିବ.

**The friendly threat** (the -ଲେ conditional of unit 19): ନ ଆସିଲେ ମୁଁ ରାଗିବି! 'if you don't come I'll be cross!' — affectionate, not rude.

**On printed cards** the language is formal: ସପରିବାର ଶୁଭାଗମନ କାମନା କରୁଛୁ 'we request the pleasure of your company with your family' (lit. we wish for your auspicious arrival).

**Answering:** yes = **ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବି**, **ମିସ୍ କରିବି ନାହିଁ**. **The trap:** **ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରିବି** 'I'll try' is heard as a polite *no*. If you mean to come, say ନିଶ୍ଚୟ; if you can't, give a reason and send a gift or wishes.

examples.native: ଶନିବାର ମୋ ଜନ୍ମଦିନ ପାର୍ଟି, ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବ।
examples.roman: sônibarô mo jônmôdinô parṭi, nischôyô asibô.
examples.en: Saturday's my birthday party — be sure to come.
Don't forget to bring back Mahaprasad.
You'll come to the reception, won't you?
If you don't come I'll be cross, I'm telling you!
We request the pleasure of your company with your family. (on a card)

dialogue.title: A wedding card
dialogue.setting: Lipsa drops by her college friend Rahul's flat in Bhubaneswar with a card for her elder brother's wedding in Puri. They're close, so they use ତୁ.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ରାହୁଲ, ଏଇଟା ନେ। ଭାଇନାଙ୍କ ବାହାଘର କାର୍ଡ!
lines.roman: Rahul, eiṭa ne. bhainaṅkô bahaghôrô karḍ!
lines.en: Rahul, here. My brother's wedding card!

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.en: Oh wow! Congrats! When's the wedding?

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ଆସନ୍ତା ମାସ ବାର ତାରିଖ, ପୁରୀରେ। ନିର୍ବନ୍ଧ ତ ଗତ ମାସରେ ହୋଇଗଲା।
lines.roman: asônta masô barô tarikhô, Purire. nirbôndhô tô gôtô masôre hoigôla.
lines.en: On the twelfth of next month, in Puri. The engagement was last month.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ବ୍ରହ୍ମପୁରର। ଶୁଣ, ତୁ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବୁ। ନ ଆସିଲେ ମୁଁ ତୋ ସହ କଥା ହେବି ନାହିଁ!
lines.roman: Brôhmôpurôrô. suṇô, tu nischôyô asibu. nô asile muṃ to sôhô kôtha hebi nahiṃ!
lines.en: From Berhampur. Listen, you have to come. If you don't, I'm not speaking to you!

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ହଉ ହଉ, ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବି, ମିସ୍ କରିବି ନାହିଁ। କିନ୍ତୁ କ'ଣ ପିନ୍ଧିବି?
lines.roman: hôu hôu, nischôyô asibi, mis kôribi nahiṃ. kintu kôṇô pindhibi?
lines.en: OK, OK, I'll definitely come, I won't miss it. But what do I wear?

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: କୁର୍ତ୍ତା ପିନ୍ଧ, ବାସ୍। କିନ୍ତୁ ବରଯାତ୍ରୀରେ ନାଚିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ!
lines.roman: kurtta pindhô, bas. kintu bôrôjatrire nachibaku pôṛibô!
lines.en: Just wear a kurta. But you'll have to dance in the procession!

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ମୁଁ ଆଉ ନାଚ? ସମସ୍ତେ ହସିବେ! ଗିଫ୍ଟରେ କ'ଣ ଦେବା ଠିକ୍ ହେବ?
lines.roman: muṃ au nachô? sômôste hôsibe! giphṭre kôṇô deba ṭhik hebô?
lines.en: Me, dance? Everyone will laugh! What would be a good gift?

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: କିଛି ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ, ଆସି ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ଦେଲେ ହେଲା। ଲୋକେ ସାଧାରଣତଃ ଟଙ୍କା ବା ଘର ପାଇଁ କିଛି ଦିଅନ୍ତି।
lines.roman: kichhi dôrôkarô nahiṃ, asi asirbadô dele hela. loke sadharôṇôtô ṭôṅka ba ghôrô paiṃ kichhi diônti.
lines.en: You don't need to — just come and give your blessings. People usually give cash or something for the home.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ଆଉ ଖାଇବା? ମୁଁ ଶୁଣିଛି ପୁରୀ ବାହାଘରର ଭୋଜି ବହୁତ ବଢ଼ିଆ ହୁଏ।
lines.roman: au khaiba? muṃ suṇichhi Puri bahaghôrôrô bhoji bôhutô bôṛhia hue.
lines.en: And the food? I've heard Puri wedding feasts are amazing.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ହଁ, ଡାଲମା, ଛେନାପୋଡ଼, ଖିରି, ସବୁ ଅଛି। ଆଉ ପରଦିନ ମହାପ୍ରସାଦ ବି।
lines.roman: hôṃ, ḍalma, chhenapoṛô, khiri, sôbu ôchhi. au pôrôdinô môhaprôsadô bi.
lines.en: Yes — dalma, chhena poda, kheer, the lot. And Mahaprasad the next day too.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.native: ବାସ୍, ମୁଁ ଆସୁଛି! ଭାଇନାଙ୍କୁ ମୋର ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା ଜଣାଇବୁ।
lines.roman: bas, muṃ asuchhi! bhainaṅku morô subhechchha jôṇaibu.
lines.en: Say no more, I'm coming! Give your brother my best wishes.

lines.speaker: Lipsa
lines.native: ନିଶ୍ଚୟ। ଆଉ ଭୋଜି ପାଇଁ ପେଟ ଖାଲି ରଖିବୁ!
lines.roman: nischôyô. au bhoji paiṃ peṭô khali rôkhibu!
lines.en: Sure. And keep your stomach empty for the feast!

culture:
**Weddings.** Most Odia weddings are still arranged between families, on an auspicious date fixed by the priest; the seasons are winter and May–June. The main steps are the **ନିର୍ବନ୍ଧ** (engagement), the turmeric ceremony **ମଙ୍ଗନ**, the arrival of the **ବରଯାତ୍ରୀ** — often late at night, with a band and lots of dancing — and the **ହାତଗଣ୍ଠି**, when the couple's hands are tied together. The bride's farewell (**କନ୍ୟା ବିଦାୟ**) is emotional, and everyone cries. Guests give cash in an envelope or something for the new home, hand it over with the right hand (or both), and bless the couple: **ଦୁହେଁ ସୁଖରେ ରୁହ**. The feast is the highlight: dalma, chhena poda, rasagola and kheer, traditionally served on leaf plates.

**Elders.** Touch the feet of elders (**ପ୍ରଣାମ**) at festivals, weddings, before exams or a journey; they'll put a hand on your head and bless you: **ସୁଖୀ ରୁହ**, **ବଡ଼ ହୁଅ**. Never use those blessing commands yourself to someone older.

**Festivals.** **Rath Yatra** in Puri (June–July) is the big one: Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra ride out on giant chariots, and the whole state watches. **Raja** (mid-June) honours the earth and women: girls swing on swings, wear new clothes and eat **ପୋଡ଼ପିଠା**. **Durga Puja** is huge in Cuttack, whose pandals are decorated with silver filigree. On **Diwali** families light lamps and call their ancestors with burning jute sticks (**ବଡ଼ବଡ଼ୁଆ ଡାକ**). On **Kartika Purnima** people float little boats at dawn in memory of Odisha's sea traders (**ବୋଇତ ବନ୍ଦାଣ**), and Cuttack holds the vast **Bali Jatra** fair. In western Odisha, **Nuakhai** (August–September) is the biggest day of the year: families gather to eat the new rice, the young greet elders with **ନୂଆଖାଇ ଜୁହାର**, and old quarrels are supposed to be forgiven. Christians, Muslims and Sikhs in Odisha's cities celebrate Christmas, Eid and Gurpurab, and neighbours drop by with good wishes.

**Birthdays** among young people mean a cake cut at midnight and a treat for friends; at home, Mum makes kheer and elders say **ଶହେ ବର୍ଷ ବଞ୍ଚ**.

tip.title: Greetings for an occasion
tip.body:
- Occasion + **-ର ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା**: ଜନ୍ମଦିନ**ର** ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା, ନୂଆ ବର୍ଷ**ର** ଶୁଭକାମନା.
- Or **ଶୁଭ** + occasion: ଶୁଭ ଦୀପାବଳି.
- Western Odisha: **ଜୁହାର** — ନୂଆଖାଇ ଜୁହାର.
- Reply: ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, **ତୁମକୁ ବି** / ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ବି!

sentences.en: Happy wedding anniversary!
Best wishes for the New Year!
Happy birthday from me!
Thanks — same to you!

sentences.native: ରଥଯାତ୍ରାର ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା! ଏଥର ପୁରୀ ଯାଉଛ କି?
sentences.roman: Rôthôjatrarô subhechchha! ethôrô Puri jauchhô ki?
sentences.en: Happy Rath Yatra! Are you going to Puri this time?
At Nuakhai the whole family gets together.
Happy Nuakhai, Grandpa!
Mum always makes something sweet on birthdays.

tip.title: 'May…': -ଉ / -ନ୍ତୁ, and elders' blessings
tip.body:
- Wish: stem + **-ଉ** — ମଙ୍ଗଳ **ହେଉ**, ପରୀକ୍ଷା ଭଲ **ହେଉ**.
- God as subject: **-ନ୍ତୁ** — ଭଗବାନ ମଙ୍ଗଳ **କରନ୍ତୁ**.
- Elders bless with commands: **ସୁଖୀ ରୁହ**, **ଦୀର୍ଘାୟୁ ହୁଅ**.
- To an elder: ଆପଣ ସୁସ୍ଥ **ରୁହନ୍ତୁ** — never command them.
tip.pattern: thing + ହେଉ  ·  ଭଗବାନ + … + କରନ୍ତୁ  ·  ସୁଖୀ ରୁହ

sentences.en: May things always go well for you.
May you be happy in your new home.

sentences.native: ଜେଜେମାଙ୍କୁ ପ୍ରଣାମ କର, ସେ ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ଦେବେ।
sentences.roman: jejemaṅku prôṇamô kôrô, se asirbadô debe.
sentences.en: Greet Grandma properly — she'll give you her blessing.

tip.title: Be sure to… / don’t forget to…
tip.body:
- **ନିଶ୍ଚୟ + future**: ନିଶ୍ଚୟ **ଆସିବ** / ଆସିବେ.
- **-ବାକୁ ଭୁଲିବ ନାହିଁ** 'don't forget to …'.
- **ଆସିବ ତ?** 'you'll come, won't you?'; **-ବାକୁ ହିଁ ପଡ଼ିବ** 'you simply have to'.
- **ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରିବି** sounds like a polite no — say ନିଶ୍ଚୟ if you mean yes.
